clue.text: Kipling's pony, a cross beast, playing 21 and 22 down

indicators.note: playing about with something shuffles it, so the two chess moves are rearranged

parts.note: 21 down is the chess move whose solution is the six-letter castling move
22 down is the four-letter chess move that ends a game

explanation.surface: A breed note on Kipling's horse, part-bred, apparently fond of chess.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is doubly cryptic: a Maltese is a kind of cross and a cat is a beast. The letters of the two chess-move answers, rearranged, give the pony.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's story of the same title is about a grey polo pony, named after a Maltese cross plus a feline beast.

clue.text: Long wait on the cards for sleeper over sleepers

indicators.note: cards get shuffled, so letters laid out on the cards are rearranged

explanation.surface: A long wait at the card table for someone who has dozed off.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LONG WAIT are rearranged. The definition plays on two kinds of sleeper: the sleeping carriage runs over railway sleepers.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental railway sleeping car is a sleeper that travels on the track's wooden sleepers.

clue.text: Time to set clock and get breath back

parts.note: a second is a small unit of time
you wind an old clock to set it going

explanation.surface: A tired runner pauses to adjust a watch and recover.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names renewed energy after exhaustion, when a runner's breathing settles again.

clue.text: See 3
Nameless impressionist with foot (errors excepted) put inside part of cathedral

indicators.note: put inside means one piece is placed within the other
lacking a name means dropping N, the usual abbreviation for name

parts.note: Renoir was a French Impressionist painter

indicators.note: excepted means left out, so the letters for the errors are removed

parts.note: a trochee is a metrical foot, one stressed then one unstressed syllable
E.E. stands for errors excepted, the disclaimer on invoices

explanation.surface: A painter, with a disclaimer about errors, is placed somewhere in a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Errors excepted' is the invoice disclaimer E.E., here read literally: the foot with its errors taken out. 'Nameless' drops N, the standard abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the area behind the high altar of a large church, a section of its architecture.

clue.text: Encouragement to beat about the bush, almost wildly

indicators.note: about means going round, so the beating word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to thump is to beat

indicators.note: wildly signals the remaining letters are scrambled
almost means the word bush loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to beat about the bush, frantically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat about the bush' looks like the idiom, but 'about' is the container: the truncated bush, scrambled by 'wildly' to BSU, sits inside the beating word.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised-thumb gesture is a sign of approval and encouragement.

clue.text: Extra to set in the comic sense

definitions.meaning: a ... tooth is an extra added to the set of teeth late in life
Norman ... was a British slapstick film comedian

explanation.surface: An extra on a film set appears alongside a comedian with a bit of sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the late-growing tooth, Norman Wisdom (a popular British film comic of the 1950s-60s), and sense in the sense of sagacity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sagacity, names a famous British comedian, and labels the late molar added to a full set.

clue.text: Get very hot water

definitions.meaning: to scorch or blaze with heat
a Scottish word for a stream or brook

explanation.surface: Instructions to heat water.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to blaze with heat, and in Scotland the noun is a small stream.

clue.text: A cock bird no friend to Israel

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
the kite is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A rooster that's an enemy of the Jewish state.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament this desert tribe were persistent enemies of the Israelites.

clue.text: Dove's top notes recited poem

indicators.note: recited means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a dove's high-pitched calls are high coos

explanation.surface: A dove's highest calls form a spoken verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A short Japanese verse form of three lines with seventeen syllables.

clue.text: False god to love, love therefore not true?

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
love again gives a second O

explanation.surface: Loving a false god, twice over, means you are not true to your faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters come from GOD, TO and two Os. The definition leans on the phrase 'too good to be true'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrealistically excellent is said to be beyond belief, so probably false.

clue.text: First to end play at an abstinent time

indicators.note: the opening letter of the play is moved to the back

parts.note: a play is a drama

explanation.surface: Put on the first play at the end of a time of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim month of daytime fasting is a period of abstaining from food.

clue.text: Early days in return of half-hearted TV city

indicators.note: return means the remaining letters are read backwards
half-hearted means one of the two central letters is lost

parts.note: Dallas was a long-running American TV soap named after the Texan city

explanation.surface: Early episodes in a rerun of a lukewarm TV series about a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' drops one of the two middle Ls of DALLAS, giving DALAS, which is then read backwards. The definition fills the blank of the phrase for youthful inexperience.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's phrase 'my salad days' means youth, a time of greenness and inexperience.

clue.text: Remove island prey of 8s' devil

parts.note: to excise is to cut out or remove
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Clear an island of the quarry of a poet's demon.
explanation.walkthrough: 8s is BURNS (8 down plus S): Robert Burns wrote 'The Deil's Awa wi' th' Exciseman', in which the devil carries off a tax officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns, himself a tax officer, wrote a song about the devil carrying off a collector of duties.

clue.text: Give boost to surrounding vulgar-sounding bully who has the franchise

indicators.note: surrounding means the boosting word goes around the rest

parts.note: to elate is to lift the spirits

indicators.note: a common accent drops initial aitches, so the bully word loses its first letter

parts.note: to hector is to bully

explanation.surface: Cheer on someone who is besieged by a crude thug with voting rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar-sounding' relies on the stereotype that coarse speech drops the initial H, so the bully word is said without it.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise here is the vote, and the body of people entitled to vote is the voting public.

clue.text: Swap larger numbers in protest from Lincolnshire town: no wind farm! no swallows!

indicators.note: the Roman numerals M and L, the two largest present, change places

parts.note: NIMBY, 'not in my back yard', is the protest of locals resisting development, such as no wind farm
Louth is a market town in Lincolnshire, England

explanation.surface: Residents of a Lincolnshire town protest against a wind farm and against birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'larger numbers' are the Roman numerals M (1000) and L (50); exchanging them is the trick. 'No wind farm!' is an example of that kind of local protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical instruction forbidding any food or drink to be taken, i.e. nothing to be swallowed.

clue.text: Obsolete institution: Act I — the goalpost must be moved

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them

explanation.surface: A stage direction for a football play: shift the goalposts in the first act.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rural infirmaries run by GPs, largely closed in Britain, are a now-outdated establishment.

clue.text: Don't talk up soldier in Indonesian region, as pack is normally used

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the region

parts.note: Aceh is a province at the north of Sumatra, Indonesia
sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An order to keep quiet about a soldier in Indonesia, with a pack of something.
explanation.definitionFit: In most card games the top-ranking cards, the ones, outrank kings, the standard way a deck is played.

clue.text: Warning not to outstay welcome I encountered in African country

indicators.note: in means the pieces are put inside the country

parts.note: Togo is in West Africa
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A traveller in Africa met someone telling them to move on.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to signal departure, a hint that guests should leave.

clue.text: Say pears and apple in tandem?

parts.note: pears said aloud is pairs, and pairs are twos
an eater is an apple for eating raw rather than cooking

explanation.surface: Fruit being shared in pairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say pears' is heard as 'pairs', which are twos; a dessert apple is an eater.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem bicycle is a machine built for two riders, so one example of the type.

clue.text: 8s' Mary's lost head in prayer

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter goes

parts.note: Burns wrote the song 'Mary Morison'; 8s is BURNS

explanation.surface: A poet's sweetheart has lost her head in prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic word for a spoken entreaty to God.

clue.text: Herb left by soldier at ease

indicators.note: left by means abandoned by, so the soldier's letters drop out

parts.note: comfrey is a medicinal herb
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers

explanation.surface: A herbalist left behind by a soldier relaxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfortable and relaxed, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Move at chess where players lose side pieces

parts.note: the cast are a play's actors

indicators.note: the side pieces of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A chess move in which a player sacrifices pieces on the flanks.
explanation.definitionFit: King and rook swap places in a special chess manoeuvre named after the rook's other name.

clue.text: Upset one in the dam

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A single person disturbed at the reservoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' wants to be a water barrier; it is a mother animal. The answer is a dialect verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern English dialect verb meaning to bother, confuse or worry someone.

clue.text: Move at chess, first of moves at the end

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter
the end takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A chess move where the first move comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: The winning attack on the king that ends a chess game.

clue.text: Title given back to archduke, being a dish

indicators.note: given back means the word is reversed

parts.note: Sir is a knight's title
Otto was the name of several Austrian archdukes, e.g. Otto von Habsburg

explanation.surface: A knighthood is returned to an Austrian aristocrat on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Awestruck, as is right and proper

parts.note: apt means fitting or proper

explanation.surface: Being in awe is the right and fitting response.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthralled or transfixed, completely absorbed in wonder.

clue.text: Strap used by blacksmith on grey mare

indicators.note: used by means the letters are found within the following words

explanation.surface: A blacksmith ties a strap on a grey horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow leather band or lace.

clue.text: Elite Spooner's drunk after fiasco

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a flop is a fiasco
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A top drinker's comment after a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the drunk word second; swapping the opening sounds of the pair gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate, of the highest class or rank.
